armingTab.allOffWarning: Every non-mandatory check is skipped. The vehicle will arm with a dead compass, no fix and an uncalibrated board.

autotune.aggrGentleBlurb: Softer response, more margin. Camera work.
autotune.aggrSnappyBlurb: Sharpest response ArduPilot will tune to.

autotuneTab.axesBody: One axis at a time takes longer but gives a cleaner result, and lets you land between them.
autotuneTab.calmAir: Fly it in calm air with plenty of room, keep the aircraft roughly in position with the sticks, and be ready to switch out. A tune saves only when you land and disarm in the mode; leaving it any other way throws the result away.
autotuneTab.disarmBody: The axes are read the moment the mode engages, so changing them in the air means tuning something other than what this screen says.
autotuneTab.downloadFailedBody: The vehicle did not send a full parameter set. Retry to pull them again.
autotuneTab.howHardBody: How aggressively the tune chases a crisp response.
autotuneTab.noAutotuneBody: AUTOTUNE_AXES is not in its parameters, so the firmware does not offer it.
autotuneTab.notLoadedBody: Autotune settings are read from the vehicle

autotuneTab.staged_other: {{count}} changes staged. Nothing is written to the vehicle until Apply.
autotuneTab.startNoMode: Switch the aircraft into AutoTune once you are flying.
autotuneTab.startWithMode: Switch into AutoTune (mode {{mode}}) once you are flying, either from the mode picker on the telemetry screen or from a transmitter switch.
autotuneTab.switchHint: To put it on a switch, use Switch Actions on the Flight Modes tab: pick the channel, then the AutoTune option. That is the same RCn_OPTION you would otherwise hunt for by number.

batteryTab.ampsPerVoltHint: Current sensor calibration. Range covers high-current industrial setups (up to 500 A/V).
batteryTab.analogPinsHint: Required for analog monitor types. Pin numbers are board-specific (Cube Orange, SITL, Pixhawk variants all differ). Set -1 to disable.
batteryTab.ardupilotNote: ArduPilot note: Thresholds are set conservatively to ensure enough battery remains for RTL. Low triggers RTL warning, Critical triggers emergency land. Unlike Betaflight, these must account for the energy needed to fly home.
batteryTab.batteryDisabledTip: Battery {{n}} monitor is disabled; select it and set a monitor type to enable
batteryTab.calibrationTip: Tip: To calibrate voltage, measure your battery with a multimeter and adjust the multiplier until readings match. For current, compare with a watt meter during a hover test.
batteryTab.capacitySliderHint: Match your battery pack capacity. Heavy-lift industrial multirotors typically 20-100 Ah.
batteryTab.chemistryHint: Select chemistry, then cell count to auto-calculate thresholds
batteryTab.helpBody: Configure your battery monitor to track voltage, current, and remaining capacity. Accurate monitoring is essential for safe flying.
batteryTab.monitoringDisabled: Battery monitoring disabled. You won't see voltage or remaining capacity!
batteryTab.notCreatedBody: ArduPilot creates the BATT{{suffix}}_ parameters on boot once a monitor type is set. Choose the monitor type above, Save All Changes, reboot the flight controller, then Refresh: capacity, thresholds and calibration will unlock here.
batteryTab.unsavedHint: You have unsaved changes. Click "Write to Flash" in the header to save.
batteryTab.voltageMultiplierHint: Adjusts voltage reading accuracy. Range covers high-voltage industrial setups (up to 200).
batteryTab.voltageThresholdsHint: When to warn and take action

boardOrientation.checkLevel: Reading level. Tip the nose up: pitch should go positive. Lift the left side: roll should go positive.
boardOrientation.checkTilted: Reading roll {{roll}}°, pitch {{pitch}}°. If the vehicle is level, the orientation or the level calibration is wrong.

boardOrientationCard.buttonsHint:
Each button turns the board 90° around the vehicle's own axes:
turn around the vertical, roll around nose to tail, pitch around side to side.
boardOrientationCard.dragHint: Drag to look around, double-click to reset
boardOrientationCard.followsVehicle: The model now follows the vehicle. Tip the real nose down: the model's nose must dip. Lower the right side: the model's right side must drop.
boardOrientationCard.goByArrow: Go by the arrow printed on your flight controller; connector positions differ between boards.
boardOrientationCard.no3d: 3D view unavailable here. Use the full list below.
boardOrientationCard.noPreset: ArduPilot has no preset for this mounting.
boardOrientationCard.notApplied: This mounting is {{param}} {{value}} ({{code}}). Not applied yet.
boardOrientationCard.setTo: Set to {{name}}. Run the level calibration next, the accel trims belong to the old mounting.
boardOrientationCard.subtitle: Turn the board on the model until it sits like the one in your vehicle. The vehicle's front stays put.
boardOrientationCard.title: Board orientation

compassCard.allDisabled: A compass is fitted but every one is switched off, so the vehicle is flying without one.
compassCard.compassHint: The magnetometer gives heading standing still, but steel structures, motor magnets and power cables bend it, and a bad reading blocks arming.
compassCard.gpsHint: Heading comes from which way the vehicle is travelling. It needs a few metres of forward movement to settle, and nothing magnetic can upset it. Normal on ground vehicles.
compassCard.noCompassBody: Most GPS modules carry one. Connect it to an I2C or CAN port, power-cycle the autopilot, and it appears here: ArduPilot only probes for compasses at boot. Until then the vehicle has no heading source, and a rover can still drive in Manual but cannot hold a heading or run a mission.
compassCard.noCompassTitle: This board has no compass of its own.
compassCard.placeDroneCan: DroneCAN node, external (GPS or CAN module)
compassCard.placeI2cExternal: I2C bus {{bus}}, address 0x{{address}}, external (usually the GPS)
compassCard.placeI2cOnboard: I2C bus {{bus}}, address 0x{{address}}, on the autopilot
compassCard.slotNote: Slot numbers are assigned in the order the drivers come up at boot and can move between reboots. The id is the device, so switch one off by its id, not by its number.
compassCard.stopUsing: Stop using this compass for heading
compassCard.title: Compasses

filesTab.deleteDirNote: Directories must be empty - non-empty directories will be rejected by the FC.

filesTab.eraseConfirmWarning: Download anything you still need before erasing.
filesTab.eraseLogsTip: Erase all flight logs on the SD card
filesTab.formatConfirmBody: This erases everything on the card, flight logs and any other files, and lays down a fresh filesystem. Use it to clear a corrupt card or leftover files from another device.
filesTab.formatConfirmParams: Your parameters are safe: they live in the flight controller, not on the card. Lua scripts and terrain data on the card will be lost.
filesTab.formatConfirmWarning: The vehicle stops logging until this finishes (a few seconds). Do not do this while armed.
filesTab.formatTip: Reformat the entire SD card (erases everything, including non-log files)

filesTab.scanCardTip: Walk the card over MAVLink-FTP and total what is on it
filesTab.sdLow: Logging stops mid-flight when free space runs out. Erase old logs before flying.
filesTab.seenOnCard: {{size}} seen on the card. Capacity is not reported over MAVLink, so subtract this from your card size for free space.
filesTab.sitlNoteBody: ArduPilot SITL exposes the FTP-virtual /APM/ tree. Files SITL actually loads (e.g. scripts) live on the host disk under the SITL working directory. They may not match what is shown here.

gpsDiagnosticsDialog.askingSats: Asking the receiver for its satellites...
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.autoConfigOff: GPS_AUTO_CONFIG is off, so the autopilot will not send these settings to the receiver.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.bridgeStep2: In u-center: Receiver, Connection, Network connection, New, then tcp://{{address}}.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.bridgeStep3: Changes there are overwritten at boot while GPS_AUTO_CONFIG is on.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.closeTip: Close and hand the GPS back to the autopilot
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.constellationsHint: Receivers limit how many constellations they track at once and ignore a set they cannot run.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.couldNotOpenPort: Could not open the GPS port
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.exclusiveWarning: The autopilot cannot use its GPS while this is open. It only opens disarmed; closing hands the GPS back.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.findAntenna: Antenna supervisor reports {{status}}: check the antenna connection.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.findNo3dFix: Satellites are visible but there is no 3D fix yet. Give it a minute with a clear view of the sky.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.findSingleSystem: Only {{name}} is being tracked. Enabling more constellations in Receiver setup usually adds many satellites.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.findSomeInterference: The receiver sees some interference. A USB cable near the module is the usual cause on the bench: test on battery only.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.findStrongInterference: Strong interference reported by the receiver. Unplug USB, and move video transmitters and ESC wiring away from the GPS.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.findWeakSignal: Used satellites average {{avg}} dBHz, good is 35 and up. Weak everywhere points at the antenna's sky view, a missing ground plane, or interference.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.jamTip: Continuous-wave jamming indicator reported by the receiver, 0 to 255
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.noConstellationSetting: This firmware has no constellation setting.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.noUbxBody: Data is arriving from the GPS port, but no satellite report. Receivers that only speak NMEA, and non u-blox receivers, cannot be diagnosed here. The u-center bridge below still passes their data through.

gpsDiagnosticsDialog.receiverSetupSub: Sent to the receiver by the autopilot at boot
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.rfWaiting: Waiting for the receiver's RF report...
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.savedReboot: Saved. The autopilot sends this to the receiver at the next reboot.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.signalStrengthSub: Carrier-to-noise per satellite in dBHz; faded bars are tracked but not used
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.signalTip: Average carrier-to-noise of the satellites used in the fix
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.sitlBody: SITL simulates a fix but not the satellites, signals or interference behind it. Connect a real flight controller with a u-blox receiver to diagnose reception.
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.sitlTitle: The simulator's GPS has no satellites to show
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.skyViewSub: Where each satellite is; filled ones are used in the fix
gpsDiagnosticsDialog.subtitle: Read straight from the receiver, through the autopilot

notifyTab.safetyBlinkHint: Outputs inhibited until the button is held

pidTuningTab.accelDesc: Max rotational acceleration per axis (deg/s²). Set by Initial Parameters and Autotune.
pidTuningTab.autotuneBody: For optimal performance, use ArduPilot's AutoTune flight mode. It will automatically tune your PID values by flying test maneuvers. Set one of your flight mode slots to AutoTune, then fly in calm conditions.
pidTuningTab.chooseToTuneEditing: Choose which one to tune, editing <m>{{set}}</m>.
pidTuningTab.downloadFailedHint: The vehicle did not send a full parameter set. Retry to pull them again.
pidTuningTab.explainDBody: Dampens overshooting and oscillation. Too high = hot motors and noise. Too low = bouncy stops.
pidTuningTab.explainFFBody: Anticipates stick movements for faster response. Useful for agile flying but can cause overshoot.
pidTuningTab.explainIBody: Keeps your aircraft on target over time. Helps fight wind and drift. Too high = slow wobbles.
pidTuningTab.explainPBody: How quickly your aircraft reacts to errors. Too high = oscillation/vibration. Too low = mushy feeling.
pidTuningTab.fetchHint: Fetch parameters from the FC to use presets and adjust values
pidTuningTab.fixedWingTip: Fixed-wing controller used in forward flight ({{params}})
pidTuningTab.presetsHint: Click to apply a tuning style
pidTuningTab.px4DualIntro: This VTOL runs separate multicopter and fixed-wing controllers.
pidTuningTab.quadPlaneDualIntro: This QuadPlane runs separate VTOL and fixed-wing controllers.

pidTuningTab.unknownSchemeHint: Use the All Parameters tab to find and edit your board's PID parameters directly.
pidTuningTab.vtolTip: Multicopter rate controller used in VTOL / hover ({{params}})
pidTuningTab.whatArePidsBody: PIDs control how your aircraft responds to commands. P = how quickly it reacts, I = how well it holds position, D = how smoothly it stops. Start with a preset!

prearmPanel.armedBody: Checks passed and the motors are live.
prearmPanel.blocked_one: {{count}} thing is in the way, newest first.
prearmPanel.blocked_other: {{count}} things are in the way, newest first.
prearmPanel.fix1: Let the board settle, or check the barometer is not in airflow.
prearmPanel.fix10: No card, or logging failed to start. Turn logging off if the vehicle has no card.
prearmPanel.fix11: Press the safety switch until the light goes solid.
prearmPanel.fix12: The receiver is not configured as ArduPilot expects; let it finish, or re-seat it.
prearmPanel.fix13: The estimator is not happy yet. Keep the vehicle still, or check the messages above.
prearmPanel.fix14: Load a valid mission, or clear the one on board.
prearmPanel.fix15: Check the rangefinder wiring and its parameters.
prearmPanel.fix16: Check the camera or gimbal is powered and reporting.
prearmPanel.fix17: The companion computer has not authorised arming.
prearmPanel.fix19: The in-flight FFT is not producing data.
prearmPanel.fix3: Wait for a 3D fix, or move where the sky is open.
prearmPanel.fix4: Run the Quick accelerometer calibration (one position, vehicle level) or the 6-point one. Level only sets trims and never clears this.
prearmPanel.fix5: A parameter is out of range; the message names it.
prearmPanel.fix6: Calibrate the radio and centre the sticks.
prearmPanel.fix7: Check the supply to the autopilot, it is outside the safe range.
prearmPanel.fix8: Charge the pack or lower the arming voltage.
prearmPanel.fix9: Calibrate or disable the airspeed sensor.
prearmPanel.ready: No refusals reported. The vehicle arms when you ask it to.
prearmPanel.skipTip: Stop checking {{name}} before arming. Only do this when the hardware is genuinely absent.

px4ArmingConfig.allActive: Every check this vehicle exposes is active
px4ArmingConfig.armSwitchButtonHint: Momentary rather than a latching switch
px4ArmingConfig.armWithoutGnssHint: PX4 inverts this one: 0 requires a position fix
px4ArmingConfig.breakersHint: PX4 protects these behind a specific unlock value rather than a simple switch, because each one removes a safety check outright.
px4ArmingConfig.disabledWarning: A disabled check does not fix the fault it was catching. Turn each one back on once the underlying problem is solved.
px4ArmingConfig.escTelemetryHint: Only for ESCs that report back
px4ArmingConfig.magStrengthHint: Catches interference and a bad calibration
px4ArmingConfig.notExposed: This vehicle does not expose the arming check parameters.
px4ArmingConfig.powerModuleCheckHint: Disable only on a bench with no power module
px4ArmingConfig.refuseUsbHint: Disable to allow arming while plugged in
px4ArmingConfig.requireMissionHint: Refuses to arm with nothing loaded
px4ArmingConfig.safetySwitchHint: Disable when no safety button is fitted

px4BatteryConfig.calibrationSubtitle: Fine-tune voltage / current and internal resistance
px4BatteryConfig.calibrationTip: Tip: To calibrate voltage, measure the pack with a multimeter and adjust until the reported voltage matches. For current, compare against a watt meter during a hover test.
px4BatteryConfig.capacityHint: Match your pack capacity. Set to -1 (Unknown) to disable mAh estimation.
px4BatteryConfig.capacityUnknown: Capacity unknown (-1). Remaining mAh will not be estimated.
px4BatteryConfig.cellCountHint: Number of cells in series. 0 = unknown.
px4BatteryConfig.cellSubtitle: Defines the full and empty endpoints PX4 uses for SOC
px4BatteryConfig.critHint: Critical warning. Usually triggers return or land.
px4BatteryConfig.emptyCellHint: Per-cell voltage treated as empty under load (LiPo ~3.5).
px4BatteryConfig.infoBody: Configure your PX4 battery estimator: cell count, per-cell voltage endpoints, pack capacity and the warning thresholds that trigger PX4 failsafes. Accurate setup is essential for safe flying.
px4BatteryConfig.lowHint: First warning. PX4 default action is typically a warning / RTL.
px4BatteryConfig.notExposed: Not exposed on this vehicle (board-defined ADC scaling).
px4BatteryConfig.rInternalHint: Per-pack internal resistance for sag compensation. -1 = automatic estimate.
px4BatteryConfig.socNote: PX4 note: State of charge is estimated from voltage between the full and empty endpoints (and internal resistance, if set). The warning thresholds below are fractions of remaining capacity.
px4BatteryConfig.sourceHint: Power Module / Analog uses the board ADC. External is a separate ADC sensor. ESCs report telemetry over the ESC link.
px4BatteryConfig.thresholdsSubtitle: Remaining-capacity fractions that trigger PX4 failsafes
px4BatteryConfig.unsavedNote: You have unsaved changes. Changes are written to the vehicle as you edit.

px4CompassCard.estimatorIgnores: A compass is fitted but the estimator is set to ignore all of them, so heading comes from somewhere else entirely.
px4CompassCard.noneCalibrated: No magnetometer has been calibrated. PX4 only fills CAL_MAG0_ID once a compass has been detected and calibrated, so connect the GPS, power-cycle the autopilot, and run the compass calibration.
px4CompassCard.priorityExplainer: PX4 picks the compass with the highest priority and falls back down the list. Setting a priority to Off is how you stop using one, and the device id is what ties the calibration to the physical sensor.
px4CompassCard.priorityTip: Higher priority compasses are preferred by the estimator
px4CompassCard.title: Compasses

px4FlightModesConfig.infoBody: Assign a PX4 flight mode to each of the 6 positions of your mode switch. PX4 splits the chosen RC channel into 6 equal ranges (slot 1 lowest, slot 6 highest) and applies the mode whose range the channel lands in. Unassigned slots are skipped.
px4FlightModesConfig.noChannel: No channel assigned. Select the channel wired to your mode switch.
px4FlightModesConfig.noSignalHint: Connect to the vehicle and move your mode switch to see the active slot highlighted live.
px4FlightModesConfig.switchChannelBody: Which RC channel selects the flight mode
px4FlightModesConfig.unsaved: You have unsaved changes. Click "Write to Flash" in the header to save.

px4LoggingConfig.noCardHint: The right setting for a board with no SD card. Without a log there is nothing to analyse after a flight, so turn it back on once a card is fitted.
px4LoggingConfig.notExposed: This board does not expose the logging parameters.
px4LoggingConfig.offSubtitle: Logging is off: nothing is written to the card
px4LoggingConfig.oldestDeleted: Oldest folders are deleted once there are more than {{count}}.
px4LoggingConfig.onSubtitle: Written to the SD card as ULog files
px4LoggingConfig.profilesHint: Logging profiles. The default set covers normal flight analysis; the rest add data for specific jobs and cost card space.
px4LoggingConfig.unlimited: Unlimited: the card fills up and the oldest logs are never removed.

px4ReceiverConfig.channelMappingHelp: PX4 reads each control function from a physical receiver channel. Set these to match how your transmitter outputs the sticks and switches. Unassigned (0) disables that function.
px4ReceiverConfig.channelMappingSubtitle: Which physical channel carries each function
px4ReceiverConfig.checkInputMode: Input mode allows RC (COM_RC_IN_MODE is RC or RC and Joystick)
px4ReceiverConfig.checkPowered: Receiver is powered and bound to transmitter
px4ReceiverConfig.checkWired: The receiver is wired to a PX4 RC input port
px4ReceiverConfig.inputModeHelp: PX4 can take manual control from an RC receiver, a ground-station joystick, or both. Choose the source that matches your setup. Most pilots use RC only. The RC loss timeout (COM_RC_LOSS_T) and failsafe action live in the Safety tab.
px4ReceiverConfig.inputModeSubtitle: How PX4 accepts manual control input
px4ReceiverConfig.rcCalibrationHelp: These values define the raw stick range PX4 maps to normalized control. Move each stick to its extremes and read the live values above, then enter Min, Max and Trim (center) here. Deadzone ignores small jitter around center. Reverse flips a channel direction.
px4ReceiverConfig.rcCalibrationSubtitle: Per-channel endpoints, center, deadzone and reverse
px4ReceiverConfig.stagedNote: Changes are staged until you Save All Changes in the header. ArduPilot-style automatic stick calibration is not available over MAVLink for PX4, so set endpoints manually using the live bars above.

px4ServoOutput.connectToEdit: Connect to a flight controller to edit actuator outputs.
px4ServoOutput.footerHint: This editor covers per-output PWM assignment. PX4 airframe geometry (control allocation, CA_ parameters) is not configured here; edit those from the Parameters tab.
px4ServoOutput.noOutputParams: No PWM_MAIN_/PWM_AUX_ output parameters were found on this vehicle. Actuator geometry (control allocation, CA_ parameters) can be edited from the Parameters tab.
px4ServoOutput.subtitle: Per-output function, range, and disarmed value

px4TelemetryRates.budgetHint: PX4 thins its streams to stay under this. Set it below what the radio can carry, not at the serial baud rate: a 57600 baud SiK link moves far less than 5760 B/s once the radio's own overhead is paid.
px4TelemetryRates.mode0Detail: The standard ground station set. What you want on the telemetry radio you fly with.
px4TelemetryRates.mode11Detail: Companion computer on a constrained link.
px4TelemetryRates.mode13Detail: Trimmed ground station set for a weak radio.
px4TelemetryRates.mode1Detail: Nothing is streamed until something asks for it.
px4TelemetryRates.mode2Detail: High rate, for a companion computer on a wired link.
px4TelemetryRates.mode3Detail: The handful of messages an on-screen display needs.
px4TelemetryRates.mode4Detail: Normal plus a few extras. Rarely what you want.
px4TelemetryRates.mode5Detail: Everything, fast. For bench work over USB, not for a radio.
px4TelemetryRates.mode7Detail: Heartbeat and little else. For a very slow link.
px4TelemetryRates.modeWarning: Changing the mode of the link you are connected through takes effect immediately and can drop messages ArduDeck is using. Config mode over USB is fine; on a radio, Normal or Low Bandwidth is what you want.
px4TelemetryRates.noInstances: No MAVLink instance parameters have been read from this vehicle yet.
px4TelemetryRates.subtitle: PX4 sets a message set and a byte budget per link, not a rate per message
px4TelemetryRates.title: Telemetry rates

rateResponsePlot.connectHint: Connect the radio and move the stick: it appears on the curve.
rateResponsePlot.fullTurn: Full stick spins a whole turn in {{turn}} s. Half stick gives {{half}} {{unit}}.

ratesTab.couldNotDetect: Could not detect ACRO_RP_RATE or ACRO_RP_P parameters on this board.
ratesTab.fetchHint: Fetch parameters from the FC to use presets
ratesTab.presetsHint: Click to apply a rate style
ratesTab.tipBody: Start with a Beginner preset and gradually increase rates as you get comfortable.
ratesTab.tipExpo: Most pilots use 180-360 deg/s for roll/pitch and 90-180 deg/s for yaw. Add expo (20-40%) if you want smoother control near center while keeping fast response at full stick.
ratesTab.tipNoExpo: Adjust the multiplier to control how aggressively the aircraft responds to stick inputs.
ratesTab.useAllParams: Use the All Parameters tab to find and edit rate parameters directly.
ratesTab.whatAreRatesBody: Rates control how fast your aircraft spins when you move the sticks. Higher rates = faster rotation.
ratesTab.whatAreRatesExpo: Expo adds a curve so small stick movements are slower.

receiverTab.calibratingBanner: Move every stick to every extreme, corners included, and every switch through every position. Release the sticks to center when done, then click Finish & Save. Channels that never move are left as they are.
receiverTab.calibrationBanner: These are the min/max/center values your flight controller learned during RC calibration. If your sticks don't reach full range or center is off, click Calibrate Radio and wiggle everything, or adjust the RCn_MIN/MAX/TRIM parameters directly.
receiverTab.checkBound: Receiver is powered and bound to transmitter
receiverTab.checkSerial: Correct SERIAL port has RCIN protocol set
receiverTab.protocolBanner: Your transmitter sends stick commands to a receiver wired to your flight controller. Select the protocol that matches your receiver. Check the label on your receiver if unsure. Auto-Detect works for most setups.
receiverTab.protocolHint: Select the receiver protocol used by your RC receiver
receiverTab.rcCalibrationHint: Current calibration values stored on the flight controller

responsePlot.moveHint: · move it and the dot follows

roverTuningTab.accelLimitHint: Auto and speed-controlled modes only, m/s² (0 = no limit)
roverTuningTab.acroTurnRateHint: A full turn takes {{s}} s at full lock
roverTuningTab.brakeOff: The vehicle coasts to a stop instead
roverTuningTab.brakeOn: Reversed output is used to slow down; needs an ESC that can reverse
roverTuningTab.brakingIntro: Most rover ESCs can drive the motors backwards to slow the vehicle. ArduPilot only does it when told it may, and only in the modes where it controls speed: Acro, Steering, Auto and Guided. In Manual the stick IS the output, so pulling back commands reverse directly and what happens then is the ESC's own brake or reverse behaviour, not this setting.
roverTuningTab.brakingLimitHint: How hard it may slow down, m/s² (0 = same as acceleration)
roverTuningTab.controlledNote: In {{mode}} the stick asks for a speed and a turn rate, and the controllers decide the outputs. Response depends on the steering and speed PIDs, not on these settings. Switch to Manual to feel the settings on this page directly.
roverTuningTab.cruiseThrottleHint: Base throttle percentage in auto modes
roverTuningTab.navIntro: These settings control how your rover follows waypoints and holds position. L1 controller determines path following accuracy - lower period = tighter turns but more oscillation.
roverTuningTab.navTip: Start with default L1 settings and only adjust if the rover oscillates on straight paths or cuts corners too much. Increase L1 Period for smoother driving, decrease for tighter following.
roverTuningTab.passthroughNote: In {{mode}} the stick is the motor output: what you set here is what you feel.
roverTuningTab.pivotIntro: For differential drive rovers that can spin in place.
roverTuningTab.pivotThresholdHint: Angle to target before using pivot turn (0 = disabled)
roverTuningTab.presetIntro: Start from one of these, then fine-tune below. The chart follows every change.
roverTuningTab.rampNone: No limit: the motors follow the stick instantly. Leave it here unless the drivetrain needs protecting from sudden reversals.
roverTuningTab.rampSluggish: {{s}} s from stop to full, and the same back: you will feel this as delay on the stick
roverTuningTab.rampTime: {{s}} s from stop to full throttle
roverTuningTab.speedIntro: Configure how fast your rover drives and how it turns. Cruise speed is used for autonomous missions, max speed is the absolute limit.
roverTuningTab.speedTip: Start with conservative speeds (2-5 m/s) and increase gradually after testing. If your rover has skid steering (tank drive), enable pivot turns for sharper maneuvering.
roverTuningTab.steerCurveCalm: Calm around centre, full lock still reaches full lock
roverTuningTab.steerCurveLinear: Linear: stick angle is steering angle
roverTuningTab.steerCurveSharp: Sharper around centre: twitchy, rarely what you want on a car
roverTuningTab.steeringIntro: Steering has its own curve, and it only shapes the stick in Manual. In Acro the stick asks for a turn rate instead.

steeringPreset.calmBlurb: Soft around centre, full lock unchanged

roverTuningTab.steeringTravelExplain: 100% is the full ±500 µs a servo accepts. This scales the whole range rather than clipping it: at 40%, full stick gives 40% and half stick gives 20%. Turn it down when the wheels reach full lock before the stick does, so the travel you have left is travel that still steers.
roverTuningTab.steeringTravelHint: Full stick puts servo {{ch}} at {{percent}}% travel ({{lo}}–{{hi}} µs)
roverTuningTab.stickCurveSoft: Soft low end: half stick gives well under half power
roverTuningTab.stickCurveStrong: Strong low end, for a motor that needs throttle before it pulls
roverTuningTab.stopSpeedHint: Outputs drop to zero under this speed (m/s), so it settles instead of hunting
roverTuningTab.throttleFeelIntro: How the rover answers the stick. The first three work in every mode including Manual; the acceleration limits only apply where the autopilot holds a speed.

throttlePreset.directBlurb: ArduPilot stock: full power, no softening

roverTuningTab.throttlePresetTip: Curve {{expo}}, top {{thrMax}}%, accel limit {{accel}} m/s². Leaves the throttle ramp alone.
roverTuningTab.topThrottleHint: Most throttle the rover will ever use (%)
roverTuningTab.turnRadiusHint: Minimum turn radius at low speeds (m)
roverTuningTab.unevenEndpoints: Endpoints are uneven around trim ({{min}}/{{trim}}/{{max}} µs), so it steers further one way than the other. Moving the slider evens them up.

safetyTab.applyPresetDesc: The following parameters will be changed on the vehicle.
safetyTab.criticalBatteryDesc: Last resort when battery is dangerously low
safetyTab.criticalBatteryWarning: <hl>Warning:</hl> Critical battery should trigger a more aggressive action than low battery (e.g. Land vs RTL). Set voltage lower than the low battery threshold.
safetyTab.criticalMahHint: Emergency action when remaining mAh drops below this
safetyTab.criticalVoltageHint: Emergency action when voltage drops below this
safetyTab.disableChecksBody: ARMING_CHECK will be set to 0. The vehicle will arm without validating sensors, GPS lock, or calibration. This can lead to flyaways and crashes.
safetyTab.fetchHint: Fetch parameters from the FC to use presets
safetyTab.gcsLostDesc: What happens when ground station disconnects
safetyTab.gcsTip: <hl>Tip:</hl> GCS failsafe requires heartbeat from ground station. If flying without GCS, leave disabled.
safetyTab.geofenceDisabledHint: Enable geofence to set altitude and distance limits. Your aircraft will RTL or land if it breaches the fence.
safetyTab.lowBatteryDesc: Protect against flying home with dead battery
safetyTab.lowMahHint: Trigger when remaining mAh drops below this
safetyTab.lowVoltageHint: Trigger when voltage drops below this
safetyTab.px4AutoDisarmDesc: Automatically disarm after landing or idle on the ground
safetyTab.px4BatteryThresholdsNote: Battery warning, critical, and emergency thresholds are configured on the Battery tab (BAT_LOW_THR, BAT_CRIT_THR, BAT_EMERGEN_THR).
safetyTab.px4DatalinkDesc: What happens when the GCS connection is lost
safetyTab.px4DatalinkHint: COM_DL_LOSS_T: delay before declaring datalink loss
safetyTab.px4DatalinkTip: <hl>Tip:</hl> Datalink failsafe needs a telemetry heartbeat. If flying without a GCS link, set the action to Disabled.
safetyTab.px4FetchHint: Fetch parameters from the FC to configure failsafes
safetyTab.px4GeofenceDesc: Limit how far the vehicle can travel from home
safetyTab.px4LowBatteryDesc: Protect against flying with a depleted battery
safetyTab.px4RcLossHint: COM_RC_LOSS_T: delay before declaring RC loss
safetyTab.px4RcLostDesc: What happens when manual control signal is lost
safetyTab.px4SafetyFeaturesBody: Configure what PX4 does when things go wrong. Failsafes can save your aircraft from flyaways and crashes. Each card maps directly to PX4 parameters.
safetyTab.rcLostDesc: What happens when transmitter signal is lost
safetyTab.safetyFeaturesBody: Configure what happens when things go wrong. Failsafes can save your aircraft from flyaways and crashes. Beginners should use the Maximum Safety preset.
safetyTab.safetyPresetsHint: Click to review and apply all settings
safetyTab.triggerPwmThresholdHint: Failsafe triggers when throttle drops below this value
safetyTab.unsavedReminder: You have unsaved changes. Click "Save All Changes" in the header to save.

sensorsTab.noTelemetry: No telemetry data received. Make sure you're connected to the flight controller.

serialPortsTab.apHowItWorks: How this works: Each row is a serial port on your flight controller. Set the protocol to match what's physically wired to that port, like RCIN for your receiver or GPS for a GPS module.
serialPortsTab.apSubtitle: Configure protocols and baud rates. Changes require Write to Flash + reboot.
serialPortsTab.noPorts: This vehicle reports no configurable serial ports.
serialPortsTab.noRcin: No serial port is configured for RC Input (RCIN protocol). Your receiver will not work unless a port is set to RCIN or the receiver is connected via DroneCAN/PPM.
serialPortsTab.portAssignmentsHint: Which serial port each function (MAVLink instance, GPS, RC, ...) runs on.
serialPortsTab.px4HowItWorks: How this works: PX4 assigns functions to ports, not protocols. Pick which port each function uses in the table below; set the port's baud rate here to match the connected device.
serialPortsTab.px4NoPortsHint: PX4 generates serial port parameters per board. Simulators (SITL) have no physical UARTs, so none exist; connect real hardware to configure its ports.
serialPortsTab.px4RebootNote: Serial configuration takes effect after saving with Save All Changes and rebooting the flight controller.
serialPortsTab.px4Subtitle: Baud rates per physical port. Changes require Save All Changes + reboot.
serialPortsTab.setupElrs: ELRS/CRSF receiver: Set one port to <hl>RCIN</hl> at <hl>115200</hl> baud
serialPortsTab.setupGps: GPS module: Set to <hl>GPS</hl> protocol at <hl>115200</hl> or <hl>230400</hl> baud
serialPortsTab.setupTelemetry: Telemetry radio: Usually <hl>MAVLink2</hl> at <hl>57600</hl> baud on TELEM1
serialPortsTab.title: Serial Port Configuration

servoOutputTab.connectToEdit: Connect to a flight controller to edit servo outputs.
servoOutputTab.duplicateHint: That is right for a vehicle with two ESCs or paired servos, and wrong everywhere else: a spare output driving nothing, or two devices fighting over one signal.
servoOutputTab.duplicateTitle: More than one output is doing the same job
servoOutputTab.subtitle: Per-channel function, range, and live output
servoOutputTab.title: Servo Output
servoOutputTab.viewAllTitle: Every channel, assigned or not, with raw values and per-output test
servoOutputTab.viewInUseTitle: The functions this vehicle has, with their travel

servoRow.mixerOverridesTooltip: ArduPlane mixer overrides this output. DO_SET_SERVO only works on Disabled (0), RCPassThru (1), or RCx_PASSTHRU (51-66) functions.

sitlBatteryCard.ignored: Not working. The setting is stored, but this airframe's simulated battery is capped at about {{v}} V and ignores anything higher, so the vehicle keeps reporting that. Restarting will not change it. To simulate a bigger pack, fly a custom frame that declares one.
sitlBatteryCard.leftFigure: The left figure is what the vehicle actually reports, so you can see whether this took effect rather than only whether it was set.
sitlBatteryCard.match: Match simulated pack to this configuration
sitlBatteryCard.overdriven: SITL's built-in airframes are calibrated around {{v}} V and their thrust scales with supply voltage, so this pack will over-drive them: hover throttle produces several times the intended thrust and a short takeoff climbs away. Only match a pack this size when you are flying a custom frame whose reference voltage suits it.
sitlBatteryCard.setCellsCapacity: set a cell count and capacity
sitlBatteryCard.subtitle: What SITL feeds the voltage sensor. Everything else here only tells the autopilot what to expect.
sitlBatteryCard.title: Simulated pack

steeringResponsePlot.connectHint: Connect the radio and move the steering stick: it appears on the curve.
steeringResponsePlot.halfStick: Half stick gives {{half}}% steering. Manual only.

stickAssignmentCard.backToStandard: Back to the standard stick assignment.
stickAssignmentCard.disarmFirst: Disarm before changing which stick does what.
stickAssignmentCard.elevatorDesc: Self-centering stick for drive and reverse, the usual rover setup
stickAssignmentCard.elevatorTip: Drive on the self-centering stick: throttle and pitch trade channels
stickAssignmentCard.noMovement: No stick movement picked up. Check the receiver is bound and try again.
stickAssignmentCard.rebootNeeded: ArduPilot only picks up a new stick assignment after a restart.
stickAssignmentCard.rebootRejected: Reboot command was not accepted. Power-cycle the vehicle instead.
stickAssignmentCard.rebooting: Flight controller rebooting. Sticks take effect when it comes back.
stickAssignmentCard.standardDesc: Channels 1 to 4 in the usual order
stickAssignmentCard.subtitle: Put a control on a different stick without touching the transmitter
stickAssignmentCard.throttleMoved: Throttle moved to the elevator stick.
stickAssignmentCard.title: Stick assignment
stickAssignmentCard.writeFailed: Could not write {{param}}. Nothing else was changed.

stickTestPanel.activeNote: Armed in MANUAL mode. Override streaming at {{hz}}Hz. Click Release to stop and disarm.
stickTestPanel.copterUnavailable: Not available on multirotors. Injecting throttle into an armed copter spins the motors. Use Motor Test to bench-check outputs one motor at a time.
stickTestPanel.errArm: Failed to arm vehicle - check Messages for PreArm reason
stickTestPanel.fcColumnHint: FC column shows what the autopilot currently reads on {{channels}} (msg 65). Green = matches your slider (override winning). Amber = mismatch. Dash = FC isn't reporting RC at all.
stickTestPanel.subtitle: Inject synthetic RC input. Mixer drives outputs as if you moved real sticks. Double-click a slider to recenter.
stickTestPanel.title: Stick Test
stickTestPanel.warnPlane: Start sets MANUAL mode and force-arms the vehicle (bypassing pre-arm checks). Bench use only - remove propellers before pressing Start.
stickTestPanel.warnRover: Start sets MANUAL mode and force-arms the vehicle (bypassing pre-arm checks). Bench use only - lift the drive wheels off the bench before pressing Start.

switchActionsSection.detectTip: Watches all channels and names the one you move
switchActionsSection.detecting: Flick a switch on your radio...
switchActionsSection.drivesTip: Makes the chosen servo output follow this switch (RCIN passthrough)
switchActionsSection.staged_one: {{count}} change staged. Nothing is written to the vehicle until Apply.
switchActionsSection.staged_other: {{count}} changes staged. Nothing is written to the vehicle until Apply.
switchActionsSection.subtitle: What each transmitter switch does: assign an aux function, or drive a servo output directly.
switchActionsSection.title: Switch Actions

telemetryRatesTab.bootDefaults: These parameters are the port's defaults at boot. A connected ground station can ask for different rates for its own session, and ArduDeck does: that is why the measured column can run well above the slider.
telemetryRatesTab.claimLink: This is the link I'm connected through
telemetryRatesTab.claimTip: Session-only rates can only be sent down the link this app is connected through
telemetryRatesTab.measuredTip: Measured on the wire right now. A GCS can ask for more than the parameter says, and ArduDeck does.
telemetryRatesTab.noBaud: No baud rate for this port, so the bar shows cost only. A radio link delivers far less than its serial baud: watch the measured column instead.
telemetryRatesTab.noPorts: No MAVLink serial ports found on this vehicle. Set a port's protocol to MAVLink2 in Serial Ports first, then come back.
telemetryRatesTab.notMeasurable: Only the link ArduDeck is connected through can be measured
telemetryRatesTab.requestedOnly: requested (not the link I am on)
telemetryRatesTab.revertTip: Drop edits you have not released yet
telemetryRatesTab.sessionRejected: The vehicle did not accept the session rates.
telemetryRatesTab.sessionRunning: Running for this session only. Nothing was written; a reboot restores the saved rates.
telemetryRatesTab.starved: Arriving slower than requested: the link is saturated
telemetryRatesTab.subtitle: How often the vehicle sends each kind of data, and what that costs on the link.
telemetryRatesTab.title: Telemetry Rates
telemetryRatesTab.trap: The trap: the number in SR0_ / MAV0_ is the MAVLink channel, not the serial port. Channels are handed out in port order, so if SERIAL7 is your only MAVLink port it is channel 0. The table below is that mapping, read from this vehicle.
telemetryRatesTab.tryTip: Applies for this session only using SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL. No parameters are written.
telemetryRatesTab.tryUnavailable: Only possible on the link this app is connected through

throttleResponsePlot.connectHint: Connect the radio and move the throttle stick: it appears on the curve.
throttleResponsePlot.noRamp: No ramp: the motors follow the stick instantly.
throttleResponsePlot.stab: A one second stab reaches {{blip}}% (full travel takes {{travel}} s).

tuningTab.autotuneBody: For best results, use ArduPilot's AutoTune flight mode. It will automatically tune your PID values by flying test maneuvers. Set one of your flight mode slots to AutoTune, then fly in a calm wind.
tuningTab.notLoadedBody: Fetch parameters from the FC to use presets
tuningTab.unsaved: You have unsaved changes. Click "Write to Flash" in the header to save.
